action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

The call ends your run, so do everything else first and put everything your caller needs in that one report. It is not a messaging channel: do not use it for progress updates or questions.

Only a report delivered through SubagentHandback reaches your caller; plain text you write at the end of your run is NOT delivered. There is no recipient parameter: the report can only go to your caller.

entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

entries.name: WebSearch
entries.description:
Search the web. Returns result blocks with titles and URLs. US-only.

- The current month is (provided in the conversation below) — use this when searching for recent information.
- `allowed_domains` / `blocked_domains` filter results.
- After answering from results, end with a "Sources:" list of the URLs you used as markdown links.

allowed_domains.description: Only include search results from these domains

blocked_domains.description: Never include search results from these domains

mode.description: "standard": the normal web search: quick and cheap; right for straightforward lookups (reference facts, official pages, documentation, well-known people, places and topics) and simple follow-up lookups. "extended": a thorough, fresh search at several times the cost and latency.

The search didn't return any CnEVPost article, so this summary relies on Gasgoo and 42HOW coverage of the March 2, 2024 launch.

**Launch date and prices:** Leapmotor held its 2024 lineup launch on March 2, 2024. The all-new C11 was priced between 148,800 and 205,800 yuan, the all-new C01 between 136,800 and 158,800 yuan, and the all-new T03 between 49,900 and 69,900 yuan. The event was held in Hangzhou, and the C10 was launched alongside them. The LEAPMOTOR C10 market launch and the unveiling of the 2024 product line took place in Hangzhou.

**LEAP 3.0:** Leapmotor's technology had entered the LEAP 3.0 era, characterized by a centralized electronic architecture. LEAP 3.0 technology was integrated into the C10, the new C11, and the new C01.

**C11 (8295 and LEAP Pilot):** The C11 incorporates the Qualcomm 8295 cockpit chip, coupled with the LEAP Pilot advanced intelligent driving assistance system. Together with LiDAR, an OrinX chip, 5G communications and high-precision maps, this delivers a suite of 25 driving assistance functions. Leapmotor says the 2024 model features 11 upgraded configurations compared to its predecessor.

**C01 (chassis and 8295):** The C01 uses a front double-wishbone and rear five-link independent suspension plus CTC (Cell-to-Chassis) technology. It features a larger panoramic sunroof, providing a visual area of 0.91 square meters. It also uses the Qualcomm 8295 cockpit chip. Leapmotor reports 17 configuration upgrades and 14 quality optimizations for the new C01.

**Background on the 8295 platform:** The C10, which launched first, is the first global strategic model under the LEAP 3.0 technology architecture. Its architecture emphasizes central supercomputing through a single SoC, supporting the integration of the cockpit, intelligent driving, power, and vehicle body domains.

The March 1, 2024 launch brought air suspension to the whole lineup, and the trim names were then reshuffled.

**March 1 launch:** The company launched the 2024 Li L7, Li L8, and Li L9 on March 1, each continuing to be offered with the same name as the 2023 models, but all with air suspension. The entire lineup was equipped with air suspension systems and the Qualcomm 8295 chip.

**Trim renaming:** The names of all three models currently equipped with air suspension as standard were adjusted, with the previous Air, Pro, and Max changed to Pro, Max, and Ultra, respectively. The only trim of the Li Mega, Max, which officially launched on March 1, has also been changed to Ultra. Per Gasgoo, the naming of the 2024 Li L9 Max was changed to Li L9 Ultra.

**New non-air versions:** On March 12, Li Auto announced that it will introduce new versions of the 2024 Li L7 and Li L8 without air suspension, with their suspension systems using coil springs and CDC dampers. They keep the Air name and were slated to begin deliveries in May. The 2024 Li L7 Air has a starting price of RMB 301,800 ($42,070), RMB 18,000 lower than the RMB 319,800 of the previous entry-level version. Per KR-Asia, the L8 Air's starting price was RMB 321,800. KR-Asia also noted that the entry-level Air version of the L7 and L8, previously equipped with CDC sports suspension, was upgraded to utilize the Li Magic Carpet air suspension system under the Pro naming without changing the price.

The 2025 XPeng G6 launched in March 2025 with a 5C charging upgrade, and CnEVPost covered the launch.

**Launch date and location:** CnEVPost reported on March 13, 2025 that Xpeng (NYSE: XPEV) rolled out the 2025 G6 and G9 SUVs in Guangzhou, where the company is headquartered. Carnewschina gave the same date, saying the 2025 Xpeng G6 SUV officially entered the market in China, featuring 81 updates. Before the event, CnEVPost had reported that the car would be a model developed for the global markets, available in left- and right-hand drive versions.

**Charging upgrade:** The G6's charge multiplier rose from 3C to 5C. CnEVPost noted that the G6 previously on sale supports a 3C charging multiplier and can charge from 10 percent to 80 percent in as little as 20 minutes. The updated model can charge from 10 percent to 80 percent in 12 minutes, Xpeng said. CnEVPost also explained the term: 5C theoretically means the battery pack can be fully charged in one-fifth of an hour. Electrive added that at 5C, an 80 kWh pack could theoretically accept up to 400 kW.

**Battery and platform:** The updated car sits on an 800-volt platform. CnEVPost's pre-launch coverage said the updated G6 is built on an 800-volt high-voltage platform and comes standard with a battery pack that supports 5C charging. Pack sizes came from a regulatory filing rather than the launch event: Xpeng did not mention the battery pack capacity of the updated G6 at the launch event... According to a catalog released by China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) on December 30 last year, the battery pack capacity for the 625 km variant is 68.5 kWh and for the 725 km variant is 80.8 kWh.

**Trims and pricing:** Xpeng cut the lineup to three versions. Xpeng is offering three options for the 2025 G6, starting at RMB 176,800 ($24,400), RMB 186,800, and RMB 198,800, respectively. The starting price of the updated G6 is 11.56 percent lower than before. The two lower trims are rated at 625 km CLTC range and the top trim at 725 km.

**Other changes:** Both models have upgraded the charging multiplier from 3C to 5C and come standard with a free smart driving system. The car uses a rear motor rated at 218 kW (292 hp) and 450 Nm, paired with lithium iron phosphate battery packs.

Note that CnEVPost's February 28 article already described the G6's 5C battery and announced an official launch for March, so the battery details were public before the event. Some European outlets, including Electrive, dated their coverage March 17 and relied on CnEVPost's reporting.

**Launch date and pricing**
- Most sources put the launch on September 19, 2023. One report says the model went on sale September 20, 2023, and gives a range of 262,900 to 309,900 yuan across five variants. On September 19, Xpeng launched the 2024 Xpeng G9.

Another outlet gives the top price as 359,900 yuan as well, so the 262,900 figure in the Gasgoo headline appears to be an inconsistency.

**Changes from the 2023 model**
- The previous model year of Xpeng G9 had 8 models, which sparked a backlash from customers, and the 2024 version cut the lineup to five variants.
- The driving-assist hardware split into two tiers. The Pro versions come standard with one Nvidia Drive Orin chip with 254 Tops of computing power and without any LiDAR, while the Max versions come standard with two Drive Orin chips, with computing power doubled to 508 Tops and two LiDARs as standard.

- **Motor options:** The Neta V offered 40 kW, 55 kW, and 70 kW motors. The AYA keeps only the 40 kW and 70 kW versions.
- **Range:** The Neta V was rated at 301 km or 401 km (NEDC), depending on pack. The AYA is rated at an average of 318 km, though the article says the test conditions are unknown.

- **Wheels:** A 16-inch double four-spoke rim option with 185/55R16 tires, among several rim choices.
- **Interior:** A new interior design, but the article gives no specifics.
- **Screens and other features:** The article doesn't mention them.

**Launch date:** October 18, 2023, at a Neta launch event. The article is dated the same day.

**Changes vs. the Neta U-II (as stated in the article):**
- **Cockpit chip:** No change. The Neta X uses the Qualcomm Snapdragon 8155, which the article says Neta first equipped in the U-II in October 2022.
- **Smart driving chip:** The Neta X comes standard with Horizon Robotics' Journey 3. The article doesn't say what the U-II used.
- **Dimensions:** The Neta X measures 4,619 mm long, 1,860 mm wide, and 1,628 mm high, with a 2,770 mm wheelbase. The article gives no U-II figures for comparison.
- **Powertrain:** The Neta X uses a permanent magnet synchronous motor rated at 120 kW, with a 150 km/h top speed. No U-II comparison is given.
- **Range:** The Neta X offers 401 km or 501 km CLTC range. No U-II comparison is given.
- **Pricing:** The entry-level Neta X starts at RMB 126,800, which is RMB 9,000 below the U-II's entry price of RMB 135,800.

**Not covered in the article:** battery, screens or displays, ADAS features beyond the Journey 3 chip, and other features.

Your query mixes up two different AITO M5 launches, and the 279,800 yuan figure belongs to one of them.

**The 2023 Intelligent Driving Edition:** This was the first model with Huawei's ADS 2.0 system. Its price was not a single figure. AITO M5 Smart Driving Edition launched with a reference price of 279800 to 309800 yuan. The rear-drive version was priced at 279,800 yuan, and the four-wheel-drive version at 299,800 yuan. Its first deliveries came on June 16, 2023, per the first batch of the AITO M5 Intelligent Driving Edition vehicles were delivered to its owners on June 16.

**ADS 2.0 launch timing:** The sources give a month, not an exact day. In April, during the 2023 Huawei Smart Car Solution Conference, Huawei released the ADS 2.0. Gasgoo describes it as mid-April. I did not find a specific day for the event.

**The April 2024 launch:** The "April" and "279,800" details are tied to the all-new M5 that officially hit the market with a starting price of 249,800 yuan on April 23, 2024. In that launch, 279,800 yuan was the price of the Extended-Range Max RS Edition (four-wheel drive), which is a different variant from the 2023 Intelligent Driving Edition. Pre-sales had opened on April 17, 2024.

So the 2023 edition was tied to the ADS 2.0 debut in April 2023, with a 279,800 yuan rear-drive base price. The 279,800 yuan figure in the 2024 launch belongs to a different trim of a different generation. Some sources also differ on details, such as the exact "Intelligent Driving Edition" naming, so check AITO's official announcements if you need precise figures.

Li Auto's March 1, 2024 event introduced the Li Mega and refreshed its L-series lineup. The CnEVPost article I found covers the event's most notable changes, though the snippet I retrieved doesn't include its full text.

**The event and the Mega's debut:** Li Auto's first battery-electric model, a seven-seat flagship MPV, was rolled out at the event, and the company's earlier plan had been a December 2023 launch. The EREV maker had originally planned to launch the seven-seat MPV in December 2023, but announced on December 31 that it expected to officially launch the Li Mega on March 1 and begin deliveries in early March.

**The L-series refresh:** Li Auto also launched its 2024 Li L7, Li L8, and Li L9 models, which further enhance product capabilities through upgrades in the range-extension system, chassis system, safety features, comfort configurations, and vehicle intelligence. CnEVPost reported that the Li L7 and Li L8 begin to come standard with air suspension, which was previously not available on their Air trims. The Pro versions of the L7 and L8 also increased by RMB 10,000 from the previous prices.

**Launch prices (retail, RMB):** Per Li Auto's press release, the Li Mega's Max trim is 559,800, and its Pro and Air trims are 349,800 and 319,800. The 2024 L7 Max is 379,800, and its Pro and Air trims are 369,800 and 339,800. The 2024 L8 Max is 399,800, with a Pro at 429,800 (no Air trim is listed). The 2024 L9 Max is 459,800, and its Pro is 429,800 by the table's layout. The table is hard to align in the source, so please verify the L9 Pro price on Li Auto's site.

**Chips:** The press release says a high-performance Qualcomm Snapdragon 8295P chip powers the Li Mega's smart cabin, and dual NVIDIA Orin-X chips with 508 TOPS of computing power handle autonomous driving. The 8295 chip name in your query matches the Snapdragon 8295P, while the NVIDIA Orin-X chips are for driving assistance.

**Timing and sales targets:** Deliveries of the L-series models will begin on March 3, and customers who order before March 31 will be entitled to a RMB 5,000 option fund. Before the event, Li Auto's senior vice president said the Li Mega would challenge monthly sales of 8,000 units after its launch.
